title: Dashboard v2: runs view from workflow beads, honest needs-you, activity feed via gc events JSONL, mail count — gc-CLI-only data plane
description:
Extend the vui city dashboard (`lisp/gascity-dashboard.el`, landed on main as
bbd6091..5ae47af) toward feature parity with the Go web dashboard's run/
activity/cost surfaces — using ONLY gc CLI `--json`/JSONL reads. NO HTTP API
calls anywhere (user directive: data plane is the gc CLI, not the supervisor
REST API). Continue the established conventions: async-first
(vui-use-async / gascity-reader-read-async, per-section independent loads,
no synchronous gc), TRAMP-safe via the reader plumbing, magit-grade inline
error surfacing.

Mayor's data reconnaissance (2026-09-24, all verified live in emacs-city):

1. RUNS VIEW (user priority 1 — "add the runs view as much as we can").
   There is NO `gc runs` CLI; the supervisor's /runs endpoint is off-limits.
   The CLI-visible proxy for a "run" is the formula-v2 workflow, which is
   fully represented in the rig bead stores:
   - A workflow root is a bead whose metadata carries `gc.graphv2_root_key`
     (and `gc.formula_name`, `gc.formula_contract: graph.v2`); its step
     beads carry the same root key and `gc.input_convoy_id`.
   - Discovery recipe (verified with `bd sql`): SELECT id, title, status,
     json_extract(metadata,'$.gc.formula_name') … FROM issues WHERE
     metadata LIKE '%graphv2-root%' — works in both rig stores. Note
     `bd query` does NOT support metadata field filters; use bd sql (it
     IS available and JSON-wrapped via `gc bd … --json`), or filter the
     full `gc bd list --json` payload client-side (stores are small).
   - Per-run progress: `gc bd show <root>` lists TRACKS/TRACKED BY (the
     full step graph, 37 steps on be-j2b); step statuses give a progress
     fraction. `gc convoy list --json` gives per-convoy progress
     {closed,total}; `gc convoy status <id>` gives the tracked-bead table
     with status/assignee columns. Implement the runs view from these:
     - Runs section (replace/extend "Work in flight"): open workflow runs
       = non-closed formula-bearing beads grouped by root key. Columns:
       run id, formula name, phase (root status), progress (closed/total
       steps via convoy progress or step-graph count), current step
       (non-closed steps with an active assignee), updated.
     - `RET` on a run: drill into a run-detail section (collapsible or
       separate buffer) rendering the step graph: step id, title, kind,
       status, assignee, from `gc bd show <root>` + the step beads.
   - Also render the input convoys feeding each run (gc convoy list
     --json, joined on gc.input_convoy_id).

2. NEEDS-YOU pending interactions (user priority 2: only if the CLI can
   supply the data, otherwise remove).
   Verified: `gc session list --json` has NO pending field; there is no
   pending-interaction CLI command (the SPA uses supervisor
   /session/{id}/pending — off-limits). THE CLI CANNOT SUPPLY IT.
   Therefore: REMOVE the `awaiting-input` plumbing? No — remove the
   DISHONEST part: the dashboard currently hardcodes `pending nil`, so
   `awaiting-input` can never fire. Replace with honest limitation:
   keep the other three reasons (errored / rate-limited / stalled — all
   derivable from `gc status` + `gc session list --json`), drop
   awaiting-input from the selector with a code comment + doc note
   ( Pending interactions need the supervisor API; out of scope by
   user directive). No fake data, no dead code paths.

3. TRANSCRIPT (user priority 3): tmux attach is the answer — do NOT
   build a transcript pane. Keep/verify the existing `t` (tmux) and
   attach paths on session rows. Nothing new beyond making sure the
   tmux target works for live sessions from the dashboard (it should
   already, via gascity-session plumbing — regression-test it).

4. ACTIVITY FEED (user priority 4): `gc events` DOES emit JSON Lines
   (verified: one DTO per line: actor, payload, run_id, seq, subject,
   ts, type; --since filters; ~500 newest default). The ga-69kj dim
   pointer stays correct for `gc event` (singular, still
   json_unsupported) but the dashboard's Activity section should now
   render real recent activity from `gc events --since <window>`
   (JSONL parse — gascity-reader already does async JSONL for peek).
   Design: last N events, columns ts/type/subject/first-line summary;
   type filter (prefix filter is fine: bead., session., convoy.,
   order.). Mind noise: order.fired/order.completed/bead.updated flood
   (944+1195 events in 2h) — default filter should probably exclude
   the chatty types or collapse them; make the filter a state var.

5. USAGE/COSTS (user priority 5): `gc costs --json` returns
   json_unsupported (verified) — so NO JSON surface for costs.
   `gc usage` does not exist as a CLI command. The only JSON-native
   option is computing per-session usage from… nothing the CLI
   exposes. CONCLUSION: usage/costs CANNOT be rendered under the
   gc-CLI-only directive. Add a dim pointer row in the cockpit
   ("costs — run `gc costs` in a shell; no JSON surface") mirroring
   the ga-69kj events-gap convention, and file a beads.el/gascity Go
   request as a bead (do not implement it).

6. MAIL unread count: `gc mail count --json` works (verified:
   total/unread). Add a cockpit header line: "mail N unread" with a
   key (`m`?) opening the existing mail reader. Provider readiness and
   waits have no CLI JSON (`gc wait list --json` exists but always
   empty in this city; readiness is HTTP-only) — skip both, note why
   in code comments.

Hard rules:
- gc CLI only. grep the new code for "url" / "http" — nothing may call
  the supervisor API. TRAMP correctness: every new read goes through
  gascity-reader async plumbing so remote works identically.
- No synchronous gc in render paths.
- Keep 380-test gate green; add ERT for new selectors (runs grouping,
  events JSONL decode, mail-count integration) with fixture payloads.
- Error surfacing: JSONL decode errors render dim inline, never blank.
- Update the dashboard footer legend for new keys/sections.
- Deliver a short report: sections added, exact CLI recipes used, and
  the two documented CLI gaps (pending, costs) with the dim-pointer
  treatment. Local commits to main; no upstream PRs; READ-ONLY on
  ~/workspace/gascity. parenmedic CLI for elisp paren issues.

title: City dashboard for gascity.el: vui.el, async-first, TRAMP — port the Go web dashboard's design to native Emacs
description:
Build a native Emacs city dashboard for gascity.el — the equivalent of the Go
dashboard's web SPA (~/workspace/gascity, internal/api/dashboardspa), rendered
with vui.el instead of React, with gascity.el's established async gc-CLI
plumbing instead of the supervisor HTTP API.

## Research already done (mayor, 2026-09-24) — build on this

### How the Go web dashboard works (~/workspace/gascity)

The dashboard is an embedded React SPA served same-origin by the supervisor
(cmd/gc/cmd_dashboard.go; internal/api/dashboardbff = backend-for-frontend,
internal/api/dashboardspa = SPA). Its routes (web/frontend/src/routes/):

- CockpitHome / AmbientHome — operator home views
- Agents + AgentDetail — roster with a "needs you" projection and per-agent
  detail with live output/transcript streaming
- Beads — board with ready/in-progress/blocked views
- Runs + FormulaRunDetail — workflow runs, run census, steps
- Activity — events feed
- Health — store/supervisor health
- Mail — operator inbox

Data comes from the supervisor REST API (internal/api/openapi.json,
/v0/city/{name}/...): status, health, agents, sessions (+transcript, +stream,
respond/wake/suspend), beads (+ready, +graph/{root}), convoys, runs (+census),
formulas, mail, events (+SSE stream), rigs, services, usage.

Cross-cutting concepts worth porting (web/shared/src/):
- work-in-flight.ts — ties in-progress beads to live worker sessions by
  parsing the trailing session handle from bead assignees
  (`<worker-role>-<session-id>`), powering a "workers active" section.
- agents/needsYou.ts — a single pure projection of operator-blocking states
  (awaiting-input | errored | rate-limited | stalled), each with one next
  action (respond | reset | nudge). Badge counts and page counts read the
  SAME selector so they cannot disagree. No clocks, no age thresholds —
  nothing can flap.
- dashboard-health.ts, alert.ts — health signals and alerts.
- structured-transcript.ts — session transcripts rendered readably.

### What gascity.el already has (reuse, don't reinvent)

- vui is already a dependency (Package-Requires vui 1.0.0; eldev resolves
  vui 1.4.0). gascity-rig.el is an EXISTING vui dashboard for one rig, with
  per-section independent async gc reads via gascity-reader-read-async —
  the exact pattern this task scales up to city level.
- gascity-reader.el: async gc CLI reads (vui-use-async compatible; processes
  auto-killed on key change), works over TRAMP.
- gascity-status.el: current magit-section status dashboard; gascity-rig.el:
  vui rig dashboard; gascity-session.el/gascity-action.el: session detail +
  agent actions (nudge/wake/suspend/kill/drain); gascity-remote.el: TRAMP
  plumbing.
- Existing shared cell formatters in gascity-tabulated.el.

## The task

Design and implement `gascity-dashboard.el` (name negotiable): a city-level
vui.el dashboard buffer showing the whole city at a glance, in the spirit of
the Go dashboard but idiomatic Emacs.

1. Study the Go dashboard sources under ~/workspace/gascity
   (internal/api/dashboardspa/web/{frontend/src,shared/src}) AND this repo's
   existing docs (DESIGN.md, docs/) before designing. Also read
   ~/workspace/gastown.el/docs/vui-design.md — prior art on vui patterns
   (use-async + refresh counter, actions plists via context, vui-table,
   collapsible sections).
2. City dashboard sections, each an independent async read so one slow or
   failing `gc --json` call never blanks the others (same rule as
   gascity-rig.el):
   - Overview/cockpit: city header (name, controller state, API URL),
     health summary, work-in-flight (in-progress beads joined to live
     sessions via assignee→session parsing, port work-in-flight.ts), needs-
     you projection for agents (port the needsYou selector's semantics:
     one reason, one next action, no clocks).
   - Agents roster (with needs-you badge/highlight) + drill into agent
     detail (reuse gascity-session detail where possible).
   - Sessions (named + live), run census / runs in flight.
   - Beads: ready, in-progress, blocked (per rig or city-wide), drill into
     bead detail; convoys.
   - Activity: recent events (respect the ga-69kj decision — gc event has
     no JSON; render the documented pointer, don't parse .gc/events.jsonl).
   - Rigs with per-rig summary rows, drilling into the existing
     gascity-rig.el dashboard.
3. Async-first: all data loads via vui-use-async / gascity-reader-read-async;
   no synchronous `gc` calls anywhere in the dashboard. Skeleton renders
   immediately with per-section spinners, then fills in.
4. TRAMP: must work on /ssh:localhost:/home/roman/bright-lights exactly as
   locally. All gc invocations go through the existing remote-aware reader
   plumbing (gascity-context pin-directory pattern like gascity-rig.el).
   Never assume local file paths. Test both access modes live.
5. Refresh: `g' refreshes in place preserving point (soft refresh);
   per-section auto-refresh where cheap. Follow gascity-rig.el's keybinding
   conventions and the shared agent-action keys (d/t/i/M/s/K/w/D/p, N/P
   section jumps) so the dashboard feels like the rig dashboard scaled up.
6. Magit-grade error surfacing: use gc's JSON error envelopes (ga-jhk9
   landed); a failing section shows its error inline, dim, with a retry
   hint — never a blank section or a swallowed error.

## Testing live in ~/bright-lights

~/bright-lights is a real, running city (supervisor-managed, mayor named
session, hello-world rig) — use it as the live target for both local and
TRAMP access modes. Use the e2e harness with timeout(1) bounds for any
batch/emacs invocation (see ga-pf3c precedent and docs/qa/ dogfood report).
Manual interactive checks in your own emacs are fine too; capture what you
verified in the report.

## Constraints

- gascity.el repo only. Do NOT touch ~/workspace/gascity (Go repo) except to
  READ it. Local commits to main are fine (polecat contract); no upstream PRs.
- Keep the existing status dashboard working; the vui dashboard is additive
  (wire it as a new entry point, e.g. `gascity-dashboard` command / a key in
  the status transient — follow existing conventions).
- If paren issues arise in elisp editing, use the parenmedic CLI
  (city-wide standing instruction).

## Deliverables

- New dashboard module(s) + tests (ERT, scripts/gate.sh green).
- A short report: sections implemented, what was reused vs new, async/TRAMP
  verification results for both access modes against ~/bright-lights,
  and known gaps (candidates for follow-up beads).
- Screenshots optional but welcome (doc/ has capture scripts).

title: capability(gc): add a pending-interactions JSON surface (gc status/session list expose no pending field)
description:
Dashboard v2 (plans/dashboard-v2) had to delete the honest "awaiting-input"/needs-you selector from the Emacs city dashboard because the data is not derivable from the CLI:

- `gc status --json` and `gc session list --json` expose no pending/awaiting-input field; pending interactions are only visible through the supervisor REST API (REST /session/{id}/pending), which gascity.el is forbidden to call by user directive.
- The dashboard therefore renders only the derivable reasons (errored, rate-limited, stalled) and a code/doc note states the limitation: "Pending interactions need the supervisor API; out of scope by user directive."

Request: add a machine-readable pending-interaction read to the gc CLI, e.g. `gc session pending --json` or a "pending" field on `gc session list --json` rows (interaction id, kind/prompt summary, session, age). Once it exists, gascity.el can restore a real needs-you section backed by CLI data instead of the current honest omission.

Related: ga-3dlf already tracks the needs-you "pending" information-model gap on the dashboard side; this bead is the CLI-side capability request. Filed by the dashboard-v2 build-basic workflow (S5, bead ga-gmbh).

title: capability(gc): add a JSON surface for gc costs (gc costs --json currently returns json_unsupported)
description:
Dashboard v2 (plans/dashboard-v2) needs a costs view, but the gc CLI has no JSON surface for costs:

- `gc costs --json` returns {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"json_unsupported",...}} (verified live in emacs-city during the dashboard-v2 workflow, root ga-uxhh).
- `gc usage` does not exist.

Per the user directive, gascity.el must not call the supervisor REST API, so the Emacs dashboard renders only a dim pointer row ("costs — run `gc costs` in a shell; no JSON surface") instead of a costs panel, and the gap is documented in the delivery report.

Request: add a machine-readable costs output to the gc CLI, e.g. `gc costs --json` returning per-session/per-agent token-and-cost totals (something shaped like {ok: true, sessions: [{session, agent, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd}], total: {...}}). Once a JSON surface exists, gascity.el can replace the dim pointer with a real costs panel in the city dashboard.

Capability requested by the dashboard-v2 build-basic workflow (S5, bead ga-gmbh).

description: Non-blocking findings from the ga-ki0j build-basic run (plans/city-dashboard/factory-run.md, Remaining Risks section). All four are small, self-contained polish items on the new gascity-dashboard.el. Gate.sh baseline is 380 tests on 5ae47af.
